title: docs(plugin-sharing): state the grantsRefused narrowing, not a spec lag
body:
Fixes #15712

Clause-②: no

Prose-only. Since #14969 (delivered by PR #15714) `@objectstack/spec` declares `grantsRefused?: number` on `SharingRuleEvaluationResult` itself, which falsified two comments in `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` that described a spec/plugin lag. The code is not wrong and is not touched: `SharingRuleReconcilePassResult extends SharingRuleEvaluationResult { grantsRefused: number }` remains a legal covariant narrowing.

Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01URLHobLUJB9K1ABV6ofdjj

## What changed

Line numbers re-derived on this branch's base `cb648cb1b` (the card read them on `22a006b26`):

| file | lines on `cb648cb1b` | the sentence #14969 falsified |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts` | 26-28 | "Additive: the six declared fields are unchanged, and a consumer typed against the spec contract keeps compiling untouched." |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts` | 145-149 | "the contract lives in `@objectstack/spec` and is another lane's to move, and every declared consumer keeps compiling against the six fields it always had. The seventh is additive…" |

Both now state the NARROWING rather than the lag: the spec declares the key OPTIONAL on purpose (an implementation that does not count refusals leaves it ABSENT, and absent is not `0`), this implementation always counts them, so the subtype REQUIRES it — which is the reason a caller holding the subtype never has to decide whether an unset key means "no grant was refused" or "this implementation does not report refusals".

The load-bearing paragraph is kept verbatim, as the card and the triage comment both demanded:

> ⛔ `grantsRefused > 0` is NOT "the pass failed". It is the pass reporting that it met a record it cannot grant on … and CONTINUED.

## The card named two instances — the sweep that makes "no others" a measurement

Three greps over `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src` (every file, tests included), each with the two known-stale blocks as its positive control:

| sweep | pattern family | hits | both known-stale blocks hit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `SharingRuleEvaluationResult\|SharingRuleReconcilePassResult\|grantsRefused`, comment lines only | 5 | yes — `index.ts:26`, `sharing-rule-service.ts:145` |
| B | `keeps compiling\|rides along\|additive\|declared fields\|declared consumer` | 10 | yes — `index.ts:27-28`, `sharing-rule-service.ts:147-148` |
| C | `@objectstack/spec` named in a comment | 8 | yes — `sharing-rule-service.ts:146` |

Plus a count/ownership sweep (`\b(six\|sixth\|seven\|seventh)\b`, `another lane\|lane's\|to move\|contract lives\|not ours`). Everything the sweeps returned beyond the two blocks was read and is unaffected by #14969:

- `sharing-rule-service.ts:151` and `:1723` — the two surviving `grantsRefused` sentences; both describe the pass's behaviour, not the spec's shape. Kept.
- `sharing-plugin.ts:1163` — "six suites in `plugin-security`" is about `buildSharingMiddleware`'s `messageTranslator` callers, a different six.
- `exec-context-annotation.pin.ts`, `bu-tree-recompute.ts`, `objects/sys-sharing-rule.object.ts`, `field-recipient.test.ts`, `logger-shapes.ts` — unrelated counts (a retired six-field exec-context shape, six hooks, six access levels, a seven-point executor contract, seven module-local logger interfaces).

Repo-wide, outside the package: `packages/client/src/index.ts` types `shares.rules.evaluate` as `SharingRuleEvaluationResult` and carries no prose about its shape; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json` names the body, not the field count. The only other text describing the lag is in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/CHANGELOG.md` (entries 563-592), which is a historical release record and correct as of the release it describes — ⛔ not edited.

## Acceptance notes

- The replaced sentence also claimed the extra key "rides along for the callers that want it — the boot backfill's aggregate and this package's own pins". `backfillRuleGrants` (`sharing-plugin.ts`) never reads `grantsRefused`; it counts reconciled rules and returns a `number`. That half was already inaccurate before #14969. Since the whole sentence was being replaced anyway, the rewrite simply does not carry the claim forward, and names the consumers that are real: this package's own pins, and `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules/:idOrName/evaluate`, which answers `svc.evaluateRule(…)` unfiltered (`rest-server.ts`, `res.json(result)`).
- Whether `SharingRuleReconcilePassResult` is still worth keeping as a named export is the same lane's judgment and is ⛔ not decided here. #15712 asks for prose only.

The restore leg is proved by a whole-tree `git status --porcelain` (empty) and by blob identity — disk `git hash-object` equals `git rev-parse HEAD:path` for both files, non-empty on both sides.

- `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.mjs` contain neither the old nor the new prose: the compiler strips comments from the JavaScript outputs, so only the two `.d.ts` / `.d.mts` files move.
- Worth recording: the `index.ts` half of this diff is a `//` comment inside an export list, and it does **not** reach the published payload at all (both markers read 0 in both builds). The `sharing-rule-service.ts` JSDoc is the half that ships.

**Clause-② — re-derived from the delivered diff, by reachability from the published entry.**

| leg | reading |

| positive control | `interface SharingRuleReconcilePassResult` is declared at `dist/index.d.ts:11920` — the touched symbol IS reachable from the published entry, so the instrument can see it |
| negative control | `declare const ENGINE_ORGANIZATION_REFUSAL_CODE` reads **0** in the same file — a module-local const in the same edited source is NOT reachable, so the instrument is not answering "yes" to everything |

⇒ `Clause-②: no`, and `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 18260` agrees independently: **exit 0** — "the clause-② declaration is readable in the fixed spelling and both carriers agree, and its diff carries no widening tell".
